sentences.text: Myriacanthus was a prehistoric species of fish with a skeleton made of cartilage.
This animal possessed a long nose and a head protected by a suit of bony plates.
Sharp spikes grew from the back of its jaw corners as part of this armor.
A solid block of cartilage anchored the top fin, while circular rings formed the spine behind the head.
Scientists estimate the creature reached a length greater than one meter based on its skull and neck size.
Louis Agassiz named the group in 1836 after finding a single spine in Jurassic rocks at Lyme Regis, Dorset.
The specific specimen used for this name had originally been identified by Henry De la Beche in 1822.
This fish belongs to the order Chimaeriformes and the family Myriacanthidae.
It serves as the foundational species for its family.
Myriacanthus lived between 205.7 and 192.9 million years ago, spanning from the Rhaetian to the Sinemurian periods.
